items.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: Until the day of the activist minister, you know such as Martin Luther King and people like that

ctx.x: So was the preacher’s message instead of asking God to change the stock market or change the white person, was it more directed at the people themselves that he was talking to and for them to do right by themselves?

Exactly. That’s what I got in church. Until the day of the activist minister, you know such as Martin Luther King and people like that, where they join in with the Civil Rights Movement, and they began to use the church and so forth, and they just completely went on against the thing and got away with it in the United States. The United States got away from the basic doctrine — the separation of church and state. It’s supposed to be something basic to America, why these people came over here, to separate the…

People seem to really value their entertainment even more during the depression, is that a fair statement? That even if they didn’t have money to spend that they would really try their hardest to still get their entertainment?
